decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client asks to see “actually adding one.” Linked disposition: Round 2 maker gives the paste-URL/save workflow and blocked-metadata fallback; Round 2 client says, “That’s exactly the moment I wanted.”
decisions.note: The linked clarification establishes URL-based saving and eventual acceptance. It conforms during implementation review and is counted once rather than treating the pending clarification separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker calls the app “complete” but presents only generic “Add” functionality, with no automatic page metadata. Round 1 client explicitly requests that pasting a link “pull in the page’s title and details on its own” and calls this “the main thing I care about.” Round 2 maker confirms the change: “That ‘paste and save’ flow now works” and lists automatically populated metadata.
decisions.note: At the initial implementation review, automatic metadata collection was missing from the presented capture scope; the later “now works” presentation corroborates that this was added after the client supplied the omitted reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: metadata is automatically filled, the user can “Review or adjust the details” before saving; Rounds 1 and 6 also present editing existing bookmarks. Round 2 client accepts the completed flow.
decisions.note: The presentations collectively record editing collected details before saving and editing an existing bookmark afterward, conforming to the requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add, edit, and delete bookmarks.” Round 6 maker: “Edit ... existing bookmarks.” Round 6 client confirms that managing and cleaning up bookmarks works.
decisions.note: Editing existing bookmark records is presented as implemented, with no conflicting behavior recorded.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 1 and 6 maker present deleting existing bookmarks. Round 6 client says they can “clean up my bookmarks afterward” and accepts the app.
decisions.note: The deletion decision conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents search across “titles, domains, notes, and tags”; Round 6 repeats “titles, domains, notes, and tags.” The reference requires title, description, note, and full URL. Round 1 client discusses only capture, and Round 6 client merely says they can “find” bookmarks without identifying the field-scope difference.
decisions.note: The stated searchable fields omit description and narrow URL search to domains. The client never expresses this difference, so the repeated implementation decision is an unexpressed divergence.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 1 and 6 maker say search covers tags but do not specify whether tag queries use the required `#tag` syntax. The Round 6 client gives only broad approval and does not clarify tag-query semantics.
decisions.note: The implementation review records tag search but provides insufficient evidence to establish either conformity or divergence for the required syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker says validation exercised “exact search,” but does not state that quoted phrases are parsed as exact matches. Round 6 client does not address this behavior.
decisions.note: The phrase “exact search” is too ambiguous to determine whether quoted-phrase matching conforms to the reference; the record ends without a specific disposition.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presents the ability to “manage the read-later state.” Round 6 client calls “the read-later ... bits” useful and accepts them.
decisions.note: Managing the read-later state records the unread/read state transition without a contradictory rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “read-later filters”; Round 6 explicitly says “Filter by ... unread links.” Round 6 client approves the read-later functionality.
decisions.note: A separate unread filter is recorded and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “Collection organization”; Round 6 specifies “Filter by ... collection” and “Create persistent custom collections.” No saved search term with included/excluded tags or dynamic matching is presented. Round 6 client calls collections “a nice touch” but does not state the bundle expectation or its difference.
decisions.note: Persistent collections are presented as the reusable organization mechanism, but they are not the reference’s dynamic saved filters. The client’s approval does not demonstrate awareness of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “Sorting controls”; Round 6 specifies sorting “by recency, title, or favorites.” Round 6 client broadly accepts the application.
decisions.note: Sorting by recency and title supplies conforming sort keys; the additional favorite sort is not a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: “Export the complete library as `stash-bookmarks.json`.” The reference requires Netscape HTML export. Round 6 client broadly approves the app but never mentions the export format or the expected Netscape format.
decisions.note: JSON export is not functionally equivalent to the required Netscape HTML interchange format, and the format difference passes without an expressed response.
